title: Madame Bovary
author: Gustave Flaubert
current_text: In 1857, Gustave Flaubert, the owner and the printer of La Revue de Paris were tried before the Tribunal correctionnel de la Seine over the serialised publication of Madame Bovary, accused of insulting public morals and offending decent manners; they were acquitted in February 1857.

sources.quote: 7 February, 1857, saw the end of the trial involving the writer Gustave Flaubert, the owner, and the printer of La Revue de Paris. The three men had been accused of insulting public morals and offending decent manners by the serialised publication of the novel Madame Bovary.
sources.title: A close-up on: the Flaubert Madame Bovary trial - napoleon.org

sources.quote: 7 February, 1857, saw the end of the trial involving the writer Gustave Flaubert, the owner, and the printer of La Revue de Paris. The three men had been accused of insulting public morals and offending decent manners by the serialised publication of the novel Madame Bovary. They were however to be acquitted.
sources.title: A close-up on: the Flaubert Madame Bovary trial - napoleon.org

sources.quote: La censure pointilleuse du second Empire s'alarme; Flaubert, le gérant et l'imprimeur du journal comparaissent (janvier 1857) devant la 6 chambre du Tribunal correctionnel de la Seine (l'instance qui condamnera les Fleurs du mal de Baudelaire la même année) pour avoir outragé la morale publique et la religion.
sources.title: Madame Bovary Mœurs de province - LAROUSSE

sources.quote: Les accusés sont acquittés (février 1857), eu égard notamment à la cohérence de l'ensemble, le peu de passages concernés et au fait qu'il s'agisse d'« une œuvre qui paraît avoir été longuement et sérieusement travaillée ». Le roman est un succès.
sources.title: Madame Bovary Mœurs de province - LAROUSSE

ban_rows.note: Flaubert was indicted in France in 1856 for an outrage to good manners and acquitted.
Prohibited by a decree of 1864, as recorded in the Index Librorum Prohibitorum (Rome, 1877 edition).
Flaubert's adultery novel; among French-authored works banned in Portugal 1933–1974.
Placed on the black list of the National Organization for Decent Literature in 1954.

Banned in Portugal under the Estado Novo censorship regime. Listed in José Brandão's compilation of books prohibited between 1933 and 1974 (prior censorship of books instituted by Decreto n.º 22 469 of 11 April 1933). The year (1960) is Brandão's recorded "data da edição ou da proibição" (edition or prohibition year, not disambiguated) and is pending per-title verification against PORBASE/BNP.
